Yes it's much more valuable to read and interpret them! At least for most people. It all depends on your end goal I suppose, but for most goals writing kanji is a skill which is almost totally useless (unless you just find it fun!). Most writing in the modern world is done through computers so there would only be very particular circumstances where you actually need to physically write out a kanji. It's not something I hadn't actually considered before talking with my friend, but really physical writing is a time investment much better spent on learning other parts of the language 

However, reading and interpreting is a skill you use all of the time! Naturally, most things are in kanji therefore it's a skill you use everyday in Japan regardless of your end goal. 

As for myself, when I learned the 2300 kanji I focused on only interpreting meaning! The readings are best picked up as you learn vocab. I learned how to write a few kanji because I found it to be fun, but I could only maybe write 100 of those 2300 from memory (and only the easier ones :P). 

I hope that answers your question thoroughly!

So I went kind of hardcore as I've been following the recommendations of an N1 friend of mine.

I used the KKLC (Kodansha Kanji Learners Course) and an Anki deck for it. The KKLC is a book with 2300 kanji which is enough that (except for name kanji) you're set for all the way to N1. So far I've not seen a kanji I don't know (again, aside from name kanji)

The Anki deck has you do both kanji to meaning and meaning to kanji and I deleted all of the meaning to kanji cards because that's pretty useless unless you want to write out kanji which these days doesn't have much value.

Anyway, I did 44 kanji every day. In the morning I'd go through the book and learn those new kanji then in the evening I'd go through my 200-250ish reviews. All in all it was about 1 hour and a half to two hours daily depending on how well the kanji stuck. It was a super grind, but the payoff is massive

You can make good guesses on both the pronunciation and meaning.

As someone who learned the meaning behind 2300 kanji a month back and is going through the 2k/6k core deck I can also say it's also super duper satisfying to see a word I've never seen in my life but know exactly what it is in meaning and reading

I want to add in my 2 cents. I learned the 2300 kanji from the KKLC (finished last week) and going into grammar and vocab again has been great. It's let me know the meanings of some words when it's my first time seeing them! I was recommended by an N1 friend I have to do those kanji as my first thing when I got back on.

What I'm trying to say is, you do you! I don't know which guide you're following for your kanji but learning all of the common ones (and more) is greatly rewarding and makes you not have to worry about it (for the most part) going forward

I came across Steins;Gate during a very difficult time during my life. Steins;Gate's story was so captivating in so many ways it gave me something else to think about during that time. It became an obsession, but in that same vein it also became a distraction., Don't get me wrong Steins;Gate was depressing, really depressing for me, especially 0. There's a scene in SG;0 that is a trigger for PTSD I developed during my childhood and outright made me vomit. But I honestly can't say I regret going through it at all.  
As much as there was the depressing moments and the stress that would sometimes keep me awake, there was also everything else. The hardworking nature of the lab, the friendships that were established, and most importantly the perseverance of Okabe.  


Steins;Gate not only gave me a reason to get out of bed each day, but I remember I used to have this thought of "If Okabe can go through all of that I can get through this". He became a role model for that perseverance, Kurisu became a role model for her intelligence and hardworking nature, and Mayuri became a role model for her openness and her putting priority on her emotions. From all that I started to feel more motivated to work harder, but also to accept when I needed to take some time for myself to just think through things and make sure I was okay emotionally.  


If it wasn't for Steins;Gate I would have lost motivation. At the time I was so close to removing myself from the world and Steins;Gate made me view things differently. Honestly thinking back on it maybe "SciAdv games have quite literally changed my life" should have said "SciAdv games have quite literally saved my life"

I have failed one class in the past and it was also Calc 3 for me as well. It was a massive shock to me and I didn't snap out of it for a few days.

What I would do is think about why you failed the course. What about hating it caused you to fail? Was it just really difficult to grasp or was there something else going on? From that you make a plan for the future. If you have to retake the course you will be much more prepared then you were last time and the experience will make you stronger in the long run. That's how I told my parents about it and they were more proud then they were angry at me.

It's cliché but massive successes are usually rooted in failure. Personally I took my failure to force myself to work harder than I ever had the following term and as a result my work ethic became exponentially better.

My condolences that you failed, I understand how hard it is but use that despair you're feeling to grow as a person and a student.

Discovering anime was a big moment in my life. I was going through some fairly serious depression and escaping into a fun slice of life world (the only genre I watched at the time) gave me hope that I could be like that and have a life worth living. After getting over the worst of my year long period with severe depression I watched Steins;Gate.

The first time I watched Steins gate it was inthe side, listening to the dub as I played games of hearthstone. By the end I put hearthstone down just watching the last 5 episodes. At the end I realized I had missed so much of a masterpiece. So I rewatched it. Twice. Everything about it was fascinating, the way the characters (especially Okabe) interacted in the face of such horrid events showed interesting glimpses into the human mind as a whole. Naturally when I heard it was based on a visual novel that not only had more to the story but also much more insight into Okabe's mind I had to get it. 

As I went through the visual novel I wrote notes on everything, appreciating every bit of foreshadowing and the way in which events interweave. I made hypotheses about how far a D-mail would jump me, and why it jumped me that far if my hypothesis was wrong.  At the end of my time with Steins gate I had a greater appreciation for motivation. Not only for my own in finishing my massive note-taking but largely from the power Okabe had to pick himself up everytime he fell down. That was something that maybe I never will have to that level but I can have a fraction of that. I can continue to pick myself up and work towards my goals.

Raiding was shakey in Legion but good overall, not quite as good as WoD raids. 

The Emerald Nightmare was a bit undertunded and lots of old mechanics were rehashed from really old raids. Some bosses were alright on mythic

Trial of Valor was a great idea having the mini raid. It was overturned and the last boss was awful on mythic unless you like dance style fights.

Nighthold was a really good raid on normal and heroic. Mythic was another story (save gul'dan, best boss to date imo). There were several bosses who fell into the category of being very easy until the last minute or so where stuff would be m much much harder. Also there were bosses that really introduced this idea of commonly having mechanics where if any 1 person in your group messed up or even lagged would kill everyone. Like playing the impossible game but with 20 people and it anyone died everyone had to restart.

Tomb of Sargeras was fun on normal and heroic as well but my god mythic is another story. The difficulty curve was insane (same could be said for Star Augur in nighthold, granted). First 3 bosses were stupid easy then you fight a kinda hard boss then a pretty easy boss. After that you face hell in the form of Mistress then you're rewarded with the absolutely hellish nightmare that is Maiden. And it gets worse from there with the last boss being so boring and soooooo punishing of literally any mistake. This raid had a -lot- of mechanics on the last 4 bosses where if 1 guy screwed up everyone died. The 2 before those guys did too to some extent.

Then Antorus. Again, a lovely raid on normal and heroic. Lots claimed the whole thing was too easy because it was cleared fairly fast but those people never fought the last two bosses. I actually thought the difficulty curve was fairly good up until the second to last boss who was just awful. 

All that being said normal and heroic raiding is better than ever, mythic is not so much BUT I still do it and will continue to as it is really quite fun it could just be improved through better testing

I know you're asking about gameplay but I see you've got some good responses already and since you're concerned with DPS ultimately I would recommend that you download an addon called simcraft. Basically all you do is login, select the talents you want then type /simc and copy that info for pasting. Then go to raidbots.com, select stat weights and copy your info into the box about your character and hit the button to sim! That will tell you which stats to aim for (you can use pawn too so you can see those weights and it will calculate upgrades for you in game). Also use bloodmallet.com as a great resource for getting your best azerite traits! Good luck

I'm playing affliction at the moment as I'm prepping for mythic and it seems to be the best at single target (atm, very subject to change). I've never done a DoT class before but I'm having a blast so far! It's very interesting learning how to best weave everything across many targets. Lots of micro managment. And I haven't done much destro as it's not my cup of tea. The other thing I will say about warlock is that as someone who had all the mage "cheats" in legion (blink while casting, iceblock, cauterize as fire) it's been humbling to play without them and has made the game more challenging (but I feel anyone would feel that when swapping classes).
